assets.note: Approved corrected-mask baseline: eye openings sit inside the white arches. The runtime overlays live copy and controls; production must separate stage, Toko, mask, props, steam and window pass.

The empty bar - STAGE_SPEC 6.3. Same room, same camera, same moment, nobody behind the counter, for the ruling that Toko is a 3D layer composited into the gap. What he stood in front of - tiled splashback, sink, shelving, stacked bowls, hanging utensils - is painted as continuing objects rather than smeared, and the counter where he worked is bare. NO UI BAND: the room runs to the bottom edge, so the stool legs and floorboards the baked band covered are visible, and the baked-screen exception in APPROVALS.md retires with this asset. NO TEXT AT ALL, which took three passes and is the point: the signboard is a blank aged board, the menu strips keep their pictograms and lose their characters, the poster is a picture, the lantern is plain, the till keys are blank. v02 still read TOKO SLOMO ... ; v03 removed the tram route number and left a glaring white destination box that looked like a mistake; v04 switches that panel off. A blank lit sign is as conspicuous as a written one.
Approved location plate; animated foliage and animals remain separate runtime layers.
Faces and hair remain combined for the slice; later extraction separates hair and hats without changing the crooked marker character.
Gameplay uses abstract reach patterns; art and UI do not teach real handling.
Use geometry and grouping only; live DOM owns actual labels and focus.
Mobile crop and command grouping reference; live DOM owns controls.

assets.presentation_rule: Only the moving presenter inside the television is 3D. Output receives limited colour, analogue softness, slight scanlines and CRT bloom. The CRT shell, lower third, newsroom props and all surrounding UI remain cut-cardstock layers.

A Kallio back yard as one diorama mesh: open ground with a brick outbuilding, chain-link and gate, a leaning lamp, pallets, a skip and bare birches. Generated as a single centred object because that is what image-to-3D is good at — a scene asked for as a scene comes back as soup. Its walkable surface is NOT at y=0; the base has real thickness and the ground must be measured from the AABB.

assets.note: Concrete skate park: graffitied ramps and a bowl, weeds through the cracks, a road along one edge. 15882 triangles, one material. CANON NOTE (updated 2026-08-28): owner ruling placed this as a real, repeatable no-stakes training battle (era1-slice-v1.json battle-hermanni-training) at a new `training`-sliceState anchor (hermanni_skatepark, map/kallio-era1-2003-v1.json) — no longer merely reachable through ?stage=. The real district is still outside the locked Era I production boundary (MAP.md 4.1); the anchor's wgs84 is nudged to sit just inside it and marked `representative-inside-production-boundary`, the same compromise already used for the Suvilahti gasworks anchor. Base colour was 2048 and the ORM map 4096; both to 1024 by art-src/tools/strip_glb_texture.py, 16.4MB to 2.8MB.

assets.note: A second HIRED body: denim jacket, khaki trousers, white striped shirt, dreadlocks, red-gold-green accents, tan boots. assets.note: Kattilahalli, the boiler hall at Suvilahti. 23272 triangles. IN BOUNDS, unlike the skate park: Suvilahti sits at Sornainen, and the map already carries a `sornainen_harbour` anchor whose roles are docks, industrial and expansion. Its sliceState is 'teaser', so placing a battle here is a content decision but not a boundary change. The hall has open sides and no floor beyond its own footprint, which is why BattleStage3D lays a concrete slab under every arena - see _build_ground_fill(). KNOWN: some textures are mirrored across opposite sides. Owner's read is that colour and lighting hide it; not attempted here. Textures were 2048 and 4096, both to 1024: 17.8MB to 3.2MB.

Older man, silver hair, glasses, moustache, navy suit, red tie. FOUND, not commissioned: it was already on the Meshy account, paid for and unused — an earlier Arvo attempt at 20794 triangles against the 20826 that shipped. Rigged for 5 credits rather than remade. Cast as Sean McCormick, who is a participant in authored encounters and had no model; an established suited man fits a family that runs bars and restaurants. Named for what it IS, not who it plays, so recasting costs nothing. 24 bones, the same skeleton as the rest of the cast. Texture 2048 to 512: 6.3MB to 1.1MB.

Heavy middle-aged man, cream work parka with orange shoulders, blue cargo trousers, orange boots. Found unused on the account and rigged for 5 credits. RECAST: he briefly stood in for Toko Slomo and was freed the moment Toko got his own model. He is now one of the `hired` bodies in battle_stage_3d.UNIT_VARIANTS — an ordinary heavy man in work clothes, which is what `hired` means. He is NOT a speaker and NOT in presenter_3d.PLACEHOLDER_SPEAKERS; this note claimed both for a while after the code had moved on, which is how a stale note misreports the cast. 18761 triangles, 24 bones. Texture 2048 to 1024, matching the polycount-is-the-lever finding in ART_BIBLE 9.7 rather than the older 512 target: 7.1MB to 0.77MB.

assets.note: Toko Slomo, the noodle chef on Vaasankatu - a named NARRATIVE.md character. White shirt with rolled sleeves, black apron, black trousers, grey hair. The gold smiling mask is CANON. 2026-08-24: remeshed at 12k from the owner T-pose with ALL APRON TEXT REMOVED, rigged, retextured to 1024. 28,765 tris and 2.0 MB down to 12,481 and 0.69 MB. baked_text is now FALSE - the apron carried TOKO SLOMO'S NOODLES over a ramen bowl and a red katakana patch, which could not be translated and had to be declared; a blank apron removes the localisation dead end and spends no polygons on lettering. Walk/run clips staged unregistered at art-library/cast3d/toko-v02-clips.glb.

Scene Club - the art-and-LAN commune at Makelansilta, owner-placed 2026-08-25, just north of Kurvi past the bridge where Makelankatu begins. Camera is LOWER than the other scenes, closer to eye height, so a full standing figure fits without cropping - owner direction: Jaska stands here and talks to camera. His table sits at the FAR WALL, mid-distance, matching the depth of the TV and LAN desks either side, with open floor left standing-room-clear in front of it for the live 3D speaker (Framing.LOCATION). v01-v03 put the table in the foreground where it cropped against the frame edge and would have cut a standing figure badly; v04 pulled it back. One background hobbyist (a LAN gamer) dresses the room; not a modelled participant. baked_text false, checked at final size: wall sketches are portraits and gesture only, monitor screens are abstract glow.

Staffed bank counter on Siltasaari - the staffed_bank site, which had been playing over the labelled placeholder. Nobody in the picture and the space above the counter left clear, per STAGE_SPEC 6.3, so the teller is a 3D layer composited into the gap rather than baked into the plate - the same ruling as the empty Toko bar. No text anywhere: the clock, brochures, screen and slips carry abstract marks only.

Harju sports pitch (Brahenkentta) - the harju_pitch site, real public place, addressPrecision public-anchor. Built from an existing unused reference photo (art-library/references/stages/stage-harju-sports-yard-night-v01.jpg) rather than invented. No people, no text - the reference's own painted graffiti lettering was replaced with abstract marks in a second pass.

Jade Lantern restaurant front - the jade_lantern_front site, fictional (faction-teaser). NARRATIVE.md's rule that members read as individuals, never a stereotype, drove the brief directly: an ordinary dignified Kallio shopfront, one plain lantern, no dragon/red-gold/pagoda theming. Four passes - a style-match correction against bank-counter-v01, then two attempts to de-text delivery crates, the second by replacing them with a plain wooden crate rather than re-editing the marked ones.

Jaska, Aatami's artist brother and moral counterweight (NARRATIVE.md), built from a likeness photo the owner supplied. 31k tris at 1024, Meshy image-to-3D task 01a03a67, rig task 01a03a69. A-POSE, NOT T-POSE, AND DELIBERATELY: a T-pose puts a narrow dark-on-dark notch between sleeve and torso that Meshy could not resolve - it bridged the gap with torn webbing geometry and baked the grey background into the shoulder seam as a visible stripe. Arms at 45 degrees over a bright cream ground opens the silhouette wide enough to reconstruct cleanly. That failure was in the MESH, not the drawing; the 2D passed every check. Glasses survive as texture rather than geometry - thin wireframe is below what image-to-3D resolves. Ten idle/talking clips staged unregistered at art-library/cast3d/jaska-v01-clips.glb.
